verses.text: Then God said to Jacob, "Arise, go up to Bethel, and settle there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau."
So Jacob told his household and all who were with him, "Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your garments.
Then let us arise and go to Bethel. I will build an altar there to God, who answered me in my day of distress. He has been with me wherever I have gone."
So they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and all their earrings, and Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.
As they set out, a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities, so that they did not pursue Jacob's sons.
So Jacob and everyone with him arrived in Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan.
There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel, because it was there that God had revealed Himself to Jacob as he fled from his brother.
Now Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. So Jacob named it Allon-bachuth.
After Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
And God said to him, "Though your name is Jacob, you will no longer be called Jacob. Instead, your name will be Israel." So God named him Israel.
And God told him, "I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation—even a company of nations—shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.
The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you."
Then God went up from the place where He had spoken with him.
So Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him—a stone marker—and he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.
Jacob called the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
Later, they set out from Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was difficult.
During her severe labor, the midwife said to her, "Do not be afraid, for you are having another son."
And with her last breath—for she was dying—she named him Ben-oni. But his father called him Benjamin.
So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
Jacob set up a pillar on her grave; it marks Rachel's tomb to this day.
Israel again set out and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder.
While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father's concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard about it. Jacob had twelve sons:
The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
The sons of Rachel's maidservant Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali.
And the sons of Leah's maidservant Zilpah were Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.
And Isaac lived 180 years.
Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Family narrative: the story of Isaac’s sons, Jacob and Esau (Genesis 25:19 to 36:43)
context.audience: Israel, named for Jacob, learning how God kept His promise through a flawed and struggling family
context.setting: God tells Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and settle there” (v.1). Jacob tells his household, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your garments” (v.2). They hand over their idols and earrings, and he buries them under the oak near Shechem (v.4). “A terror from God” falls on the cities, so no one pursues them (v.5). At Bethel Jacob builds an altar to the God who answered him “in my day of distress” (vv.3, 7). Deborah, Rebekah’s old nurse, dies there (v.8). God appears again, confirms the name Israel, and says, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply… kings shall descend from you” (vv.9-12). Jacob sets up a stone pillar and pours out a drink offering (v.14). On the road south Rachel dies giving birth: she names the baby Ben-oni, son of my sorrow, but his father calls him Benjamin, son of the right hand (vv.16-18). She is buried “on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)” (v.19). Reuben sleeps with Bilhah (v.22), and the chapter lists Jacob’s twelve sons (vv.22-26). Jacob comes home to his father at Mamre, and Isaac dies at 180; “his sons Esau and Jacob buried him” (vv.27-29).
context.custom: Earrings were often worn as amulets, and gold earrings later went into the golden calf (Exodus 32:2-4). Changing clothes and washing were signs of making a fresh start before meeting God (Exodus 19:10). A man who took his father’s concubine was claiming his father’s place (2 Samuel 16:21-22); Reuben loses the rights of the firstborn for it (Genesis 49:3-4; 1 Chronicles 5:1). Benjamin is the only son of Jacob born in Canaan.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 36 lists the descendants of Esau, the people of Edom, and the chiefs and kings of their land.
context.timelineBible: Jacob keeps the vow he made at Bethel (28:20-22): God has brought him back, and he worships there. Matthew hears Rachel weeping for her children at Bethlehem when Herod kills the boys there (Matthew 2:18, quoting Jeremiah 31:15). Rachel’s tomb is still honored on the road to Bethlehem.

translation.meaning: Foreignness: literally, gods of the foreigner. Jacob’s household must be cleansed of other gods before it meets the LORD at Bethel.
God Almighty, El Shaddai, the name God gave Himself to Abraham (17:1). Its exact meaning is debated; the Greek and Latin Bibles took it as all-powerful.
Son of the right hand, the place of honor and strength. Jacob refuses to let his son carry the name of his mother’s death.

gospelParallels.note: We are the temple of the living God; come out and be separate.
You turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God.

otBackground.note: Rachel weeping for her children; they will return.
Throw away the foreign gods that are among you.
Rachel’s tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin.

overview.summary: Jacob purifies his household and returns to Bethel, where God confirms the name Israel and the promise; Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and Isaac dies at 180.
overview.settingLine: From Shechem to Bethel, Bethlehem and Mamre.

history.t: The list of the tribes is complete with Benjamin.
Esau and Jacob bury their father together, as Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham.

customs.t: Worn as charms and given up with the idols.
Wine or oil poured out to God.

archaeology.t: The present building near Bethlehem dates mainly from Ottoman times.
Beitin has remains from the Middle Bronze Age onward.

overview.discussion: Before going back to Bethel, Jacob’s family buried their idols (v.4). What would I need to put away before going back to the place where I first met God?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters. Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

peoplePlaces.d: Returns to Bethel and keeps his vow

currentImage.caption: Rachel’s Tomb near Bethlehem in a 19th-century photograph (Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam). Genesis says Rachel was buried “on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)” and Jacob set up a pillar on her grave (35:19-20).
